'''Yuga Shrine Hongū''' ({{lang|ja|由加神社本宮}}) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine}} located on [[Yuga Mountain]] in the Kojima area of southern {{ill|Kurashiki|en|Kurashiki}}, {{ill|Okayama Prefecture|en|Okayama Prefecture}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Independent Shinto shrine|lt=Independent Shinto shrine|lt=Standalone Shrine|ja|単立神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Standalone Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q7882536|redirects to 単立|2=ja|3=単立|2=ja|3=単立|redirects to 単立|2=ja|3=単立|}} unaffiliated with the {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Association of Shinto Shrines|qq=}}. Its modern status under the shrine Ranking system is a former {{ill|Ken-sha|ja|県社|qid=Q90139226}}{{efn|Ken-sha|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q90139226|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

== Overview ==
Mount Yuga has been a center of {{ill|Iwakura rock|ja|磐座信仰|lt=Iwakura faith}} since ancient times. In 733 CE, the monk {{ill|Gyōki|ar|جيوكي|de|Gyōki|es|Gyōki|fr|Gyōki|ja|行基|ko|교기 (승려)|pl|Gyōki|ru|Гёки|zh|行基|qid=Q1136664}} enshrined an {{ill|Ekādaśamukha|en|Ekādaśamukha|qid=Q11404731|lt=Eleven-faced Kannon}} statue here, establishing a religious complex that merged Shinto and Buddhism under the name '''{{nihongo|{{ill|Yuga Daigongen|ja|瑜伽大権現|en|Yuga Daigongen}}|瑜伽大権現}}''' (Yuga Great Incarnation). According to the history of {{ill|Kumano Shrine (Kurashiki)|ja|熊野神社 (倉敷市林)|qid=Q11568940|lt=Kumano Shrine}}, five disciples of {{ill|En no Gyōja|de|En no Gyōja|es|En no Gyōja|fa|ان نو گیوجا|fr|En no Gyōja|he|אן נו גיוג'ה|it|En no Gyōja|ja|役小角|ko|엔노 오즈누|pl|En-no Gyōja|ru|Эн-но Гёдзя|sh|En no Gyōja|uk|Ен-но-Ґьодзя|zh|役小角|qid=Q198946}}, a prominent ascetic, brought Kumano deities from {{ill|Kii Province|cs|Provincie Kii|de|Provinz Kii|es|Provincia de Kii|eu|Kii probintzia|fa|ولایت کیئی|fr|Province de Kii|gl|Provincia de Kii|id|Provinsi Kii|it|Kii (provincia)|ja|紀伊国|ko|기이국|lt|Kijo žemė|nl|Kii (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Kii|pt|Província de Kii|ru|Кии (провинция)|simple|Kii Province|sk|Kii (provincia)|sr|Провинција Киј|th|แคว้นคิอิ|tr|Kii (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Кії|vi|Tỉnh Kii|zh|紀伊國|zh_min_nan|Kii-kok|qid=Q864053}} and established Kumano Shrine in the northern foothills of Mount Yuga. They later founded Nachi Shrine on Mount Yuga as one of the "New Kumano Three Mountains."

From the mid-{{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, the shrine became a place of worship for the {{ill|Ikeda clan|en|Ikeda clan|qid=Q2975277|lt=Ikeda clan}}, rulers of {{ill|Bizen Province|en|Bizen Province}}. The Ikeda clan sponsored the construction of the shrine’s buildings and nearby {{ill|Yugasan Rendaiji|ja|蓮台寺_(倉敷市)|en|Yugasan Rendaiji|lt=Rendaiji}}.

The shrine is located in a bustling {{ill|Monzen-machi|ja|門前町}}, with numerous souvenir shops and food stalls. During the New Year period, the shrine attracts many visitors. A specialty of Mount Yuga is the locally famous "ankoro mochi" (sweet red bean rice cakes).

In the {{ill|Meiji period|en|Meiji period}}, the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri}} (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) policy split Yuga Shrine from Rendaiji Temple. Yuga Shrine now has 52 branch shrines across western Japan.

After {{ill|World War II|en|World War II}}, the shrine and temple informally resumed cooperation, with temple monks conducting prayers at the shrine. However, Yuga Shrine formally resumed independent religious activities in 1997, leading to a dispute with Rendaiji over property and operations.

In the Edo period, a practice known as "dual pilgrimage" emerged, encouraging worshippers to visit both {{ill|Yuga Daigongen|ja|瑜伽大権現|en|Yuga Daigongen}} and {{ill|Konpira Gongen|en|Konpira Gongen}} in {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province}}.
== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines Hikosa no Oshinomikoto, Kamunaobi-no-Kami, Daigongen (Honji Buddha: {{ill|Amitābha|en|Amitābha|qid=Q236242|lt=Amitābha}}, {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|en|Bhaisajyaguru|qid=Q854773|lt=Yakushi Nyorai Medicine Buddha}}), and others, including:
* {{ill|Hikosachi no Mikoto|ja|彦狭知命|lt=Hikosa-no-Oshinomikoto}}
* {{ill|Kamuna'obi|ja|神直日神}}
* {{ill|Yuga Daigongen|ja|瑜伽大権現|en|Yuga Daigongen}} (associated Buddhas: {{ill|Amitābha|en|Amitābha|qid=Q236242|lt=Amitābha}}, {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|en|Bhaisajyaguru|qid=Q854773|lt=Yakushi Nyorai Medicine Buddha}})
* {{ill|Sanuki Inbe clan|ja|手置帆負命|lt=Teokihobufu no Mikoto}} 
* {{ill|Ame-no-Minakanushi|es|Ame-no-minaka-nushi-no-kami|fa|آمه-نو-میناکانوشی|fr|Ame-no-Minakanushi|id|Ame-no-Minakanushi|it|Ame-no-Minakanushi|ja|天之御中主神|mni|ꯑꯃꯦ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯅꯀꯅꯨꯁꯤ|pl|Amenominakanushi|ru|Амэноминакануси|simple|Ame-no-Minakanushi|uz|Ame-no Minakanusi|zh|天之御中主神|qid=Q2842779|lt=Ame-no-Minakanushi}}
* {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞鳴命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}
* {{ill|Ukanomitama|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Kami|ja|倉稲魂命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukanomitama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ウカノミタマ}}
* {{ill|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|ja|Sugawara no Michizane|2=ja|3=菅原道真|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sugawara no Michizane|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q382005}}
* {{ill|Watatsumi|ja|大綿津見命|lt=Watatsumi-no-Mikoto}}

*

== Cultural Properties ==
* '''main hall''' – Built in the early Edo period, it is designated as an {{ill|Important Cultural Property of Okayama Prefecture|ja|岡山県指定重要文化財}} (1961).<ref name=岡山県文>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pref.okayama.jp/cgi-bin/bunka/culture/controller/client/resultDetail.cgi?id=174 |title=main hall of Yuga Shrine |publisher=Okayama Prefecture |accessdate=2018-06-24}}</ref>

== Access ==
* '''By Car:''' About 15 minutes from [[:en:Seto-Chuo Expressway|Seto-Chuo Expressway]]'s {{ill|Mizushima Interchange|en|Mizushima Interchange}}.
* '''By Taxi:''' About 15 minutes from {{ill|Kojima Station|en|Kojima Station}} on the {{ill|Seto-Ohashi Line|en|Seto-Ohashi Line}}.
* '''By Bus:''' A limited {{ill|Shimoden Bus|en|Shimoden Bus}} service runs from Kojima Station to Yuga Shrine (twice daily). However, buses do not operate on weekends, holidays, or during the New Year period.
